notes:
Account overview: Saffron Stacksmith builds a VS Code extension for multi-language teams; focus on low-latency inline completions, stream-first UX, and per-developer rate limiting.

Recent activity / timeline:
- 2024-09-02: Intro call (Maya) — brief product demo, initial interest in streaming completions + model pinning.
- 2024-09-18: Follow-up: sent architecture doc + draft SLA (drive link).
- 2024-10-08: Prod demo with SE (Daniel) — validated end-to-end latency ~60ms median with hosted model; asked about 30-40ms targets. (FF-20241008-873)
- 2024-10-29: Security sync — SSO requirements, audit logging scope, retention windows discussed (FF-20241029-121).
- 2024-11-05: Email thread re: pricing commitment levels and burst capacity for peak coding sessions.

Use-case / requirements summary (from product + eng):
- Primary workload: VS Code extension providing inline suggestions & streaming completions for JS/TS, Python, Go.
- UX: streaming token-by-token updates to editor; ability to cancel/rewind suggestions quickly.
- Latency SLO: target 30-50ms per token for single-user requests; P95 < 150ms across team.
- Throughput: average 2-4 concurrent editors per seat during team coding sprints; spike handling for 150 concurrent devs across org.
- Model needs: prefer open models + ability to pin model versions per release (model versioning + rollbacks).
- Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to trade cost for latency for core product users; needs optimizer suggestions.
- Routing/fallback: automatic fallback to smaller quantized models on Dedicated or local cache if hosted capacity constrained.
- Auth / limits: org SSO (SAML), per-developer token limits, API keys for extension instances, clear rate-limit headers.
- Security: strong audit logs, configurable retention, EU data residency for subset of customers, KMS integration for secret material.

POC scope and acceptance criteria:
- 2-week POC (extension branch) that demonstrates: streaming completion with <70ms median token time, model pinning UI working, and basic per-user throttling.
- Security: SSO smoke test + audit log entry verification for sample sessions.
- Metrics: token-cost report and latency breakdown visible in console.

Quotes / call notes (shorthand):
- "If we can get token-level latency to ~40ms it's a product win" — Saffron CTO.
- "Need to ensure offline/poor-network behavior is graceful — fallback to local cached suggestions" — lead eng.

Open questions for Redwood:
- Exact semantics of per-user rate limits (burst vs sustained).
- Whether model pinning supports staged rollouts (canary) across extension versions.
- Data residency mapping for EU customers (which data is persisted).

Next steps (short):
- SE to deliver POC build by 2024-11-20.
- Security to provision SSO test account (pending).
- Pricing follow-up scheduled 2024-11-22.
